subject: Private deployment residency matrix & standby network triggers
messages:
From: Helene Sørensen <helene.sorensen@nordicbankab.se>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T07:45:00+02:00
Subject: Private deploys: residency constraints + warm-standby question

Hi Ava / Jonas,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We have two parallel asks from our compliance and infra teams: one is a hard requirement that EU production traffic and persisted KV caches for European customers remain in EU jurisdiction; the second is a resilience requirement from our APAC office — they want an automated warm-standby in APAC that can accept traffic within a 5 minute RTO but must never hold EU customer persisted data at rest.

Can Redwood outline a recommended deployment pattern that meets both constraints? Specifically:
- A short residency matrix that maps which artifacts may be replicated cross-border (KV cache prefixes, model binaries, logs, telemetry)
- A network / failover trigger model so APAC failover does not inadvertently create EU-residency violations

We'd like this as an internal deliverable we can share with our Security Architecture Council next Thursday (2027-09-16). If you can provide a short ops checklist and a one-page diagram, that would be ideal.

Attachments: none from our side.

Best,
Helene Sørensen
Head of Cloud Security — NordicBank AB

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helene Sørensen <helene.sorensen@nordicbankab.se>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, PrioM Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Private deploys: residency constraints + warm-standby question

Helene — thank you, noted.

High level follow-up: Redwood can support your constraints with a two-tier private deployment pattern we typically call "EU-active / APAC-warm-standby". Key guarantees we will aim to document for you:

1) Data residency enforcement: persisted KV caches and any customer PII logs will be write-only in the EU cluster. Read-replication to APAC is blocked for any EU tenant IDs.
2) Model binaries: model artifacts (non-user data) may be synced to APAC for fast cold-starts; we treat these as non-residency-limited assets but can sign them with EU-only gating if you prefer.
3) Network failover triggers: we will propose a controller that uses health and jurisdiction checks — a failover can only be initiated if (a) EU tenant set has been drained, or (b) there is an explicit emergency override approved by NordicBank security.

I asked Jonas and Priyom to draft the residency matrix and the ops triggers. Laura will own the compliance write-up for your Security Council.

I'll share a first-pass residency_matrix_v1.xlsx and a one-page trigger diagram by EOD tomorrow.

Ava Chen
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: residency_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-09-13T09:28:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Private deploys: residency constraints + warm-standby question

Folks — draft technical notes and a short checklist below; I'll attach a fuller playbook. High-level constraints and recommended controls: 

- KV cache handling:
  * Use tenant-scoped namespaces. EU tenants -> EU-only namespace with enforcement at the runtime admission layer.
  * Replica suppression: the control plane will block KV replication replication requests for EU namespaces unless a signed override token is provided.

- Networking / failover:
  * Health windows: 3x probe failures (configurable) across primary region -> then controller initiates controlled drain.
  * Controlled drain flow: stop accepting new EU-tenant requests in APAC, instruct EU-active nodes to flush ephemeral caches to EU-only persistent store, then switch routing for non-EU traffic to APAC.
  * Circuit breaker: automatic cutoff if any EU resident KV writes are detected in APAC nodes (this should never happen but acts as a safety net).

- Operational triggers and human approvals:
  * Routine failover: automated based on latency/packet loss thresholds — requires pre-authorized signed policy.
  * Emergency failover: requires at least two approvers from your security ops team + Redwood on-call.

I've attached: standby_network_triggers_v0.3.pdf (diagram + sequence) and operational_handoff_notes.txt (runbook items).

Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: standby_network_triggers_v0.3.pdf; operational_handoff_notes.txt

Helene — attaching the three artifacts Jonas and I promised. Quick summary for your Security Council packet: 

1) Residency matrix (residency_matrix_v1.xlsx): enumerates artifacts (tenant metadata, KV caches, model weights, logs, telemetry) and allowed replication paths. EU tenant data remains write-only in EU.
2) Standby network triggers (standby_network_triggers_v0.3.pdf): sequence diagram showing controlled drain, gating checks, and circuit-breaker behaviors.
3) Operational handoff notes (operational_handoff_notes.txt): one-page checklist for your on-call runbook (who to call, HSM/KMS considerations, rollback steps).

Next steps we propose:
- You run the doc through the Council on 2027-09-16.
- If Council requests changes, send comments inline on the Google Doc link we shared.
- We can schedule a tabletop test the following week (suggest 2027-09-22) to simulate an APAC warm-standby failover without any EU data leaving the EU cluster.

If it helps, Laura will prepare a short compliance note that explicitly lists controls mapping to GDPR articles and our SOC 2 controls.

Thanks — Ava
